sections.h2: What speeds up a house sale in Hamilton Township, Atlantic County?
sections.html:
Three things set the pace here: a resale inspection arranged through the township, a clear tax payoff and a deed recorded at the courthouse in Mays Landing. This page covers the Atlantic County township around Mays Landing, a different place from the Hamilton near Trenton.

The Census Bureau estimates 28,845 residents for July 1, 2025, up 5.0 percent from its 2020 base. Owners live in 70.7 percent of homes, and the typical owner-occupied value is $246,200. Listings range from suburban streets in the developed east to rural lots in the pine forest of the west, and a cash buyer who takes the house as it stands removes loan approval and repair negotiations from that timeline.

sections.h2: What sets Hamilton Township apart from other Atlantic County towns?
sections.html:
Hamilton Township has the most land of any municipality in New Jersey at 110.90 square miles, and it calls itself the state's largest municipality. Counting water as well, only Galloway Township is bigger. Mays Landing, the Atlantic County seat since the county formed in 1837, sits inside the township with the census-designated places of McKee City and Mizpah.

A great deal of that land is protected. The township belongs to the New Jersey Pinelands National Reserve, and the Pinelands Commission regulates the western three-quarters, which remains pine forest. The eastern quarter is a Regional Growth Area where development is allowed and encouraged, and most residents live there, near the Hamilton Mall and other shopping centers.

  • Mays Landing: 5,603 residents in 2020, home to the county courthouse complex.
  • McKee City: 9,758 residents in 2020, the largest census-designated place in the township.
  • Lake Lenape and the Great Egg Harbor River: recreation areas, with the Lake Lenape parks covering over 2,000 acres.

If the house sits on or near undeveloped land, ask the township planning and zoning office whether the parcel lies inside the Pinelands Area before you describe what a buyer could add or build.

sections.h2: How did Hamilton Township grow into what it is now?
sections.html:
The township was incorporated on February 5, 1813, from parts of Egg Harbor and Weymouth townships. Its early economy followed the Great Egg Harbor River: a shipyard and trading post opened near Babcock Creek at Mays Landing in 1756, and more than 200 vessels were built along the river between 1830 and 1880.

The population stood at 6,017 in 1960, 16,012 in 1990 and 27,484 in 2020. Retail is part of the economy, with more than 3,000,000 square feet of stores including Hamilton Mall, Consumer Square and Hamilton Commons, and a winery on a 57-acre vineyard.

sections.html:
The average home here was billed $5,931 in 2025, on a general rate of 3.520 per $100. The table sets the state and Census numbers side by side.

sections.h2: What inspection happens before a Hamilton Township resale?
sections.html:
Township fire inspectors check smoke and carbon monoxide detectors before a house is resold or reoccupied, and requests go through the online title transfer inspection portal linked from the Fire Prevention page. The state Uniform Fire Code requires a smoke alarm certificate for one-family and two-family houses that are sold, leased or reoccupied, and only the municipality issues it.

The construction office at the township hall, 6101 Thirteenth Street in Mays Landing, schedules its own inspections in person or by fax and does not accept phoned-in requests. A certificate stays valid for six months, so ask for the inspection once you have a contract and a closing date.

  • Working smoke alarms on each floor, the basement included, and near sleeping areas.
  • A carbon monoxide alarm where the code calls for one.
  • Sealed ten-year smoke alarms when you replace old ones.

Code Enforcement also responds to property maintenance complaints, so clear any open issue before you list.

sections.h2: How do assessments and appeals work in Hamilton Township?
sections.html:
Appeals go to the Atlantic County Board of Taxation at 5909 Main Street in Mays Landing. A petition must arrive before the close of business at 4 p.m. on April 1, because a postmark does not count, and petitions about added or omitted assessments follow the same rule on December 1. The 2026 April deadline has passed.

The board accepts filings online through MyNJAppeal.com, where evidence can be uploaded until seven days before the hearing. Assessment cards usually arrive in late January, and the board publishes lists of usable comparable sales. The test is whether your assessment exceeds what the house would sell for.

Request a payoff figure from the township tax collector before closing, and check the parcel in the county's property assessment search before you set a price.

sections.h2: What will a Hamilton Township seller pay, and where is the deed filed?
sections.html:
The state's Realty Transfer Fee falls on the seller at recording. The state's own example for a $325,000 deed is $1,910, and the township's average 2025 sale of about $312,000 sits in the same bracket, with a rate that begins at $2.00 per $500.

The Atlantic County Clerk records deeds at the Historic Court House Complex, 5901 Main Street in Mays Landing, which lies inside the township. A satellite office serves Atlantic City at 1333 Atlantic Avenue. Make recording and transfer fee checks out to the Atlantic County Clerk's Office, and send any nonresident Gross Income Tax prepayment to the State of New Jersey Division of Taxation.

  • GIT/REP-3 residency certification for New Jersey residents.
  • Gross Income Tax prepayment for nonresident sellers, set at 2 percent of the price or more.
  • A deed prepared by the closing attorney or title company.

sections.h2: Which schools, highways and buses serve Hamilton Township buyers?
sections.html:
Hamilton Township Schools teach prekindergarten through eighth grade in three schools: Shaner Memorial, the George Hess Educational Complex and William Davies Middle School. Older students attend Oakcrest High School in the township, part of the Greater Egg Harbor Regional High School District. Atlantic Cape Community College's Mays Landing campus has operated since 1968.

A 14-mile stretch of the Atlantic City Expressway crosses the township with three interchanges, and U.S. Routes 40 and 322 and Route 50 cover other directions. NJ Transit buses 502 and 553 reach Atlantic City, and the 315 runs between Cape May and Philadelphia.

faqs.q: Is an inspection mandatory before selling in Hamilton Township, Atlantic County?
faqs.a: Yes. Township fire inspectors check smoke and carbon monoxide detectors before resale, and requests go through the online title transfer inspection portal. State law requires the certificate for one-family and two-family houses.

faqs.q: Where does a Hamilton Township deed get recorded?
faqs.a: At the Atlantic County Clerk's Office, 5901 Main Street in Mays Landing, inside the township. A satellite office is at 1333 Atlantic Avenue in Atlantic City.

faqs.q: What is the assessment appeal deadline here?
faqs.a: April 1 at 4 p.m., with December 1 as the date for added or omitted assessments. Filing works online, and a postmark does not satisfy the deadline.

faqs.q: Is this the same Hamilton as the one in Mercer County?
faqs.a: No. They are separate municipalities in different counties, each with its own tax board, clerk and inspection office. This page covers the one around Mays Landing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house that sits in the Pinelands?
faqs.a: Yes. Pinelands rules govern what can be built, so ask the township planning and zoning office what the parcel's zone allows before you advertise additions or lot splits.
